pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #16 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How many cardinal points are there on a compass? (1 mark)
   A. Four
   B. Eight
   C. Six
   D. Two

2. Which direction lies between north and west? (1 mark)
   A. South-west
   B. North-east
   C. North-west
   D. South-east

3. Which of these people is most likely to use a compass? (1 mark)
   A. A cook
   B. A sailor
   C. A tailor
   D. A baby

4. Which is the smallest county in Kenya by area? (1 mark)
   A. Narok
   B. Mombasa
   C. Kitui
   D. Turkana

5. Which country lies to the west of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Tanzania
   B. Uganda
   C. Somalia
   D. Ethiopia

6. Which of these should a good county sketch map have? (1 mark)
   A. A recipe
   B. A photograph of the teacher
   C. A title
   D. A picture of a tractor

7. Which of these is a way of caring for a river? (1 mark)
   A. Planting trees along its banks
   B. Cutting trees at the bank
   C. Throwing rubbish into it
   D. Washing cars in it

8. Which of these uses the water of a river to make electricity? (1 mark)
   A. A market
   B. A hydroelectric power station
   C. A church
   D. A school

9. What do we call a place where a river falls over a cliff? (1 mark)
   A. Valley
   B. Waterfall
   C. Plateau
   D. Plain

10. During the dry season herders in dry areas often do what? (1 mark)
   A. Collect rainwater
   B. Plant maize
   C. Sell umbrellas
   D. Move animals to find water and grass

11. Which clothing is most suitable in the cold season? (1 mark)
   A. Swimming costumes
   B. Light shorts only
   C. Sweaters and jackets
   D. Sandals only

12. In many parts of Kenya, when do the short rains usually come? (1 mark)
   A. January only
   B. March to May
   C. June to July
   D. October to December

13. Thimlich Ohinga is found in which county? (1 mark)
   A. Mombasa
   B. Migori
   C. Turkana
   D. Nairobi

14. Who built Fort Jesus? (1 mark)
   A. Nobody built it
   B. The Kenyan government in 1990
   C. The Portuguese
   D. The British in 1950

15. What is the name of the organisation that looks after most museums in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Kenya Airways
   B. Kenya Ports
   C. National Museums of Kenya
   D. Kenya Power

16. Who helps at weddings and funerals in many communities? (1 mark)
   A. Only the government
   B. Nobody
   C. Only the police
   D. Neighbours and relatives

17. What does interdependence mean? (1 mark)
   A. People needing and helping each other
   B. People doing everything themselves
   C. People living alone
   D. People fighting

18. Which pattern describes people living along a road or river in a line? (1 mark)
   A. Circular
   B. Clustered
   C. Linear
   D. Scattered

19. Why do herders in dry areas not live crowded in one place? (1 mark)
   A. They move with animals to look for water and grass
   B. They do not use water
   C. They have no families
   D. They dislike roads

20. On a dot map where one dot means 500 people, an area has 4 dots. How many people live there? (1 mark)
   A. 2,000
   B. 20,000
   C. 400
   D. 4,500

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain what harambee is and give one example of what it can be used for. (2 marks)

22. Name the five countries that border Kenya. (5 marks)

23. A bar graph shows sub-county A has 40 thousand people and sub-county B has 25 thousand. Find the total population of the two sub-counties. (3 marks)

24. State the direction that is opposite to each of these: north and east. (2 marks)

25. Draw a simple chart showing three workers, what each gives, and what each needs. (3 marks)

26. Explain what interdependence means and give one example. (3 marks)

27. Give three reasons why historic built environments are important. (3 marks)

28. Name the four seasons in the county. (2 marks)

29. Write a short note to invite a resource person to talk about a historic place in your county. Include the reason and the date. (5 marks)

30. Give two reasons why some areas are densely populated. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #16 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Four
   There are four cardinal points: north, east, south and west.

2. C — North-west
   North-west is between north and west.

3. B — A sailor
   Sailors use compasses to find direction at sea.

4. B — Mombasa
   Mombasa covers the smallest area of all the counties.

5. B — Uganda
   Uganda is Kenya's western neighbour.

6. C — A title
   A good map has a title, a north arrow and a key.

7. A — Planting trees along its banks
   Trees hold the soil and keep the water clean.

8. B — A hydroelectric power station
   Hydroelectric stations use falling river water to make electricity.

9. B — Waterfall
   A waterfall is where a river drops over a steep edge.

10. D — Move animals to find water and grass
   Grass and water become scarce, so herders move.

11. C — Sweaters and jackets
   Warm clothing keeps us comfortable when it is cold.

12. D — October to December
   The short rains usually come between October and December.

13. B — Migori
   Thimlich Ohinga is in Migori County.

14. C — The Portuguese
   The Portuguese built the fort more than 400 years ago.

15. C — National Museums of Kenya
   The National Museums of Kenya manages many museums.

16. D — Neighbours and relatives
   People help by cooking, lending items and comforting.

17. A — People needing and helping each other
   Interdependence means we depend on each other.

18. C — Linear
   Linear means in a line.

19. A — They move with animals to look for water and grass
   Herding needs large areas of pasture.

20. A — 2,000
   4 x 500 = 2,000.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Harambee is people pulling together to solve a problem, for example to build a school or a clinic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Uganda, Tanzania, Ethiopia, South Sudan and Somalia.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each country.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: 65 thousand, which is 65,000 people.
   Working / marking points: 40 + 25 = 65 thousand. 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for 65 thousand, 1 mark for 65,000.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: The opposite of north is south. The opposite of east is west.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct opposite.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: farmer gives food and needs clothes; teacher gives learning and needs food; driver gives transport and needs repairs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct row.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Interdependence means people depend on and help each other. For example, a farmer grows food and a trader sells it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example, 1 mark for showing both sides need each other.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: They teach us history, they give us identity and pride, and they bring tourists and income.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Hot, cold, dry and rainy.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for all four, 1 mark for two or three.

29. (5 marks)
   Answer: A polite greeting, the name of the person, the reason for the invitation, the date and time, and a thank-you at the end.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of the five parts.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Good rain and fertile soil for farming, and jobs and services in towns. Accept water or good roads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.
